Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testAxisPreceding` exercises XPath axis preceding and node() selection on a DOM model. The current bug report hypothesizes that the method in `DOMNodePointer.java` around line 120 incorrectly restricts the node() test to only match element and document nodes, while it should match any node type.

Investigation of `DOMNodePointer.testNode(Node, NodeTest)` at lines 117-167 reveals the relevant code. When the test is a `NodeTypeTest` with node type `Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE` (representing node()), the code only returns true if the node type is either `Node.ELEMENT_NODE` or `Node.DOCUMENT_NODE`. This matches exactly the condition the bug report calls out as wrong.

The XPath node() test should match all node types, but currently DOMNodePointer restricts it to elements and documents, which can cause tests involving preceding or other axes combined with node() to fail or behave incorrectly (such as in the provided test case).

None of the recent bug reports gathered provide additional relevant insight beyond similar node matching or XPath interpretation issues. Hence, the root cause for the failure is the restrictive condition in `DOMNodePointer.testNode` at lines 146-148, which means node() won't match text nodes, comments, processing instructions, or other node types, contrary to XPath specifications.

Fixing this by allowing node() tests to return true for all node types should resolve the failing test and the issue described.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
